newsitem.title: CHINA: China says Taiwan's tight controls hurt trade.
newsitem.headline: China says Taiwan's tight controls hurt trade.

text.p: Taiwan's tight controls on trade with China were hurting economic ties but links could be helped by the return of Hong Kong to Chinese rule in 1997, the official Xinhua news agency said on Tuesday.
"If the Taiwan authorities continue to pursue a policy of tight controls, circumstances will not be good for trade contacts," the news agency said.
This was "something that we do not want to see", the agency quoted Wang Hui, an official of the Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation, as saying.
Taiwan has rejected Chinese overtures to lift a ban on direct trade and transport links imposed at the end of the Chinese civil war in 1949.

But Wang said he believed the return of Hong Kong to Chinese rule on July 1, 1997, and the possible entry of Beijing into the World Trade Organisation (WTO) would provide good opportunities for developing economic and trade exchanges between China and Taiwan.
Wang did not elaborate but analysts have said that Taiwan may adjust its China trade policy after Hong Kong reverts to Chinese rule.

Indirect trade between Taiwan and China was worth $17.76 billion in the first 10 months of 1996, up 2.6 percent compared with the same period of the previous year, the island's Board of Foreign Trade said at the weekend.
Most of Taiwan's trade with China goes through Hong Kong and the return of the British colony to Beijing would create direct trade links.
China has been trying to join the WTO but so far has failed to meet the organisation's requirements. Xinhua did not say how WTO status would help China's trade with Taiwan.
Wang said trade between China and Taiwan took a downturn this year due to the island's attempt to break out of diplomatic isolation.
China conducted war games and missile tests near Taiwan in March in the run-up to the island's first direct presidential elections.
Bilateral trade began recovering in July, Wang said but gave no further details.
China regards Taiwan as a rebel province and has sought to push the island into diplomatic isolation.
